sentences.text:
A R KADRI(7330) for the petitioner(s) No. 1,2 MR URVESH PRAJAPATI, for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MS CM SHAH, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE HASMUKH D. SUTHAR  Date : 16/04/2024
ORAL ORDER 1.
Learned counsel for the petitioners, on instructions, does not press this petition qua petitioner No.1 - Pethabhai Magankumar Parmar @ Parth Patel.
Hence, present petition stands disposed of as not pressed qua petitioner No.1.
2. Learned advocate Mr. Urvesh Prajapati states that he has instructions to appear on behalf of the original complainant and thereby, seeks permission to file his Vakalatnama, which is granted.
3. RULE.
Learned advocates waive service of note of rule on behalf of the respective respondents.

4. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and since it is jointly stated at the bar by learned advocates on both the sides that the dispute between the parties has been resolved amicably,
this matter is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

5. By way of this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter Pethabhai Magankumar Parmar @ Parth ... vs State Of Gujarat on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30901746/
1 referred to as "Cr.P.C."), the petitioner No.2 has prayed to quash and set aside the complaint NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/1829/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024 undefined being FIR No.I-50 of 2017 registered with Sola High Court Police Station, Ahmedabad, for the offences under Sections 376, 406, 420, 323, 506(2) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, Section 25(1)(1) of Arms Act and Section 135 (1) of Gujarat Police Act and all the consequential proceedings arising therefrom.
6.

sentences.text:
Learned advocates for the respective parties submitted that during the pendency of proceedings,
the parties have settled the dispute amicably and pursuant to such mutual settlement, the original complainant has also filed an Affidavit, which is taken / placed on record.

In the Affidavit, the original complainant has categorically stated that the dispute with the petitioner/s has been resolved amicably and that he has no objection, if the present proceedings are quashed and set aside since there is no surviving grievance between them.
7. So far as applicant No.2 is concerned, he is facing charge of abetment.
Perusing the complaint, it appears that the allegation levelled against applicant No.2, who was friend of applicant No.2, qua abetment only.
Allegations qua rape and administering threats and shown revolver/arm to the complainant are against applicant No.1 and he has committed offence of rape.

So far allegation against applicant No.2 under Sections 323 and 506(2) of IPC is concerned, after two months of the incident, he has given threat to settle the dispute with applicant No.1 and he has made an assault by kick and fist blows.
Thereby, applicant No.2 has not abetted in the offence of rape.

8. Having heard learned advocates on both the sides and considering the facts and circumstances of the case as also the principle laid down by the Apex Court in the cases of (i) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, (ii) NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/1829/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024 undefined Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab, reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, (iii) Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 31, (iv) Manoj Sharma Vs. State & Ors., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 190 and (v)
Narinder Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported in 2014 (2) Crime 67 (SC), in the opinion of this Court, the further continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioner/s in relation to the impugned FIR would cause unnecessary harassment to the petitioner/s.

Hence, to secure the ends of justice, it would be appropriate to quash and set aside the impugned FIR and all consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C..
9.
In the result, the application is allowed.

The impugned complaint being FIR No.I-50 of 2017 registered with Sola High Court Police Station, Ahmedabad as well as all consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof are hereby quashed and set aside qua petitioner No.2 only.
